identity.description: Podio: a web-based no-code work platform for workspaces, apps, items, tasks and contacts (product matches the task).
identity.identity_notes: developers.podio.com documents the Podio API. Wikipedia describes Podio as a web-based no-code platform; its history section says Citrix acquired it in 2012. The Wikipedia page says Progress Software completed the purchase of ShareFile and Podio on Oct 31, 2024, which was seen in one source only. Progress's own MCP docs cover Podio as well.

auth.oauth_flows: Two-step authorization code flow for most clients (user is sent to Podio, then code is exchanged at the token endpoint). One-step flow with user email and password is only for trusted clients. App authentication uses an app ID and app token from the app's Developer link.
auth.token_refresh: Access tokens last 8 hours by default according to a secondary summary; the primary doc did not state lifetime or refresh behavior. Unknown from primary source.
auth.scopes_notes: Scope list not verified. The app auth page says an app-authenticated client can only access that specific app.

access.production_restrictions: Some destructive operations (such as deleting workspaces or apps) need an increased trust level; rate-limit exceptions also need a request to Podio support with the API key client_id. Podio asks developers to review its Terms of API use.

api.rate_limits: Two limits: Limit A for resource-intensive operations and Limit B for all other operations. Exceeding them returns errors. Paid accounts can buy an API Add-on for higher limits. Exact numbers not stated in the sources read.
api.limitations: The docs page lists resource groups but does not describe CRUD operations or response format. Sources did not explicitly say REST or JSON. Some resource descriptions on the docs page are garbled, such as Flows.

open_questions: Protocols (REST/JSON) are not explicitly stated in the fetched docs; verify on the API reference.
Full CRUD operations per resource (read_ops/write_ops) were not listed in the docs; the API reference needs a direct check.
Exact rate-limit numbers for Limit A and Limit B were not found.
Whether a free developer account can create an API key without admin approval or a paid plan was not explicitly confirmed; the FAQ says the API is available on free accounts.
Access token lifetime (8 hours per a search summary) and refresh-token behavior are not confirmed from the primary OAuth doc.
Whether community MCP servers are GitHub-hosted was not confirmed; the listed community options are third-party hosted services.
Current owner of Podio: Progress Software acquisition (Oct 2024) rests on a single Wikipedia source.
